question_put_to_a_human: What are chapters 785 through 794 about, in one sentence? Put to a human before this file was written, as it has been put before every writer since 595. No human has answered it for any block from 595 onward. No writer answers it for them. It is recorded here unanswered and it stays open until somebody answers it.
family: THE FAMILY FOR THIS BLOCK IS A GOOD REPAIR AND WHAT THE PERSON DOES WITH IT AFTERWARDS. Somebody finds something wrong in their own place and means to deal with it their own way. Somebody else arrives, takes the second half, and does it properly. THE REPAIR IS GOOD AND IT STAYS GOOD. THE METHOD IS GOOD AND IT HAS NO HOLE IN IT. THE FAULT IS NOT IN EITHER METHOD AND IT IS NOT IN THE REPAIR. THE FAULT IS IN THE PERSON. The person does not leave the job alone. They lean on it, they stop doing the other thing that was keeping the rest of it right, they go straight back to what they were doing before, they do it again themselves because they do not like it, they keep a hand on it, they carry on the one habit the repair was meant to make unnecessary, or they hand it on to somebody else and it gets done the other way round. Every chapter ends with a repair that is better than it was and a person who is worse off in relation to it, and nobody in any of the ten can say whether the repair was worth it.
family_why_this_and_not_the_three_neares: In 755 to 764 the visitor's method was the fault and the host's own was what stayed. In 765 to 774 the adopted method was right for the job and had a hole in it, and the fault was in the method. In 775 to 784 the adopted method had no hole in it and was still wrong, and the fault was in the repair itself, in the position or the choice or the moment. IN 785 TO 794 THE METHOD IS RIGHT, THE REPAIR IS RIGHT, AND THE PLACE IS RIGHT, AND THE PERSON UNDOES THE VALUE OF IT WITH THEIR OWN HANDS AFTERWARDS. A later writer may not go back to a fault in a method, a hole in a method, or a fault in a repair.

0788 she is out on her own front path at number nine in the cold for the whole of the middle of the day, and a bay of that path is the whole of the job

0794 she is in her own yard and her own shed at number ten from the middle of the morning until it is going dark, and a sack of gravel that has been standing there since May is the whole of it

cards.0785: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has the rear step of her van packed on one chip and a hinge that has failed, and means to pack it on two chips and fit a new hinge; the woman who books work takes the step off, gets the whole bed down onto the chassis rail and fits a new hinge with the pin out and a new pin in; the step is right, and within the month she is packing it again herself with whatever is to hand, because the step is not the thing that is wrong with the way she loads.
cards.0786: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has four feet of bare frost wall at the coal shed end and a heap of loose brick in the grass, and means to lay four of them on it and be done; her sister takes that four feet down to the bottom of the footing, packs the bottom of the hole and both sides of it with broken wall and stone chippings trodden down in layers, and puts back every brick that came out of it with none of the four from the heap, which 0767 has already found to be the wrong thickness and the rest of them broken, bedding them dry with every perpend packed with chippings and the coping bedded on the top of it, and no mortar anywhere in it; the wall is better than it has been since it was built and does not move where the old one moved, and three weeks later the old woman takes four bricks off the top course and puts them back her own way, because she does not like the look of a wall with the chippings showing in it.
cards.0787: At the unit a man in his early forties has a gate post that leans between two turns of wire and means to dig it out, drive it back down plumb and put another turn of wire on it; the woman from two doors down digs it out, gets it down to the bottom of the hole, packs the bottom with broken stone stood on end and hardcore rammed in and packs the sides of the post with the same in layers, pins it plumb with two hardwood wedges and cuts them off flush, and puts the two turns of wire back where 0769 had them, one a hand's width under the top and one a hand's width up off the ground, the wire being rusted into the post in about a dozen places and coming off with a cold chisel; the post does not move at all now, and inside a month he has stopped leaving the gate standing where the frost left it and shuts it hard every time he comes through it, and by the spring the post has begun to go over again at the height of his hip, and it goes because of what he did to it and not because of what she did.
cards.0788: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has the middle flag of her front path bedded high at the door end and dropping to the rail, and means to lift it and put a bit of sand under it; the woman who does her shopping takes the bay up and relays it on a new bed to the level of the flags either side; the flag is true and stays true, and the tub goes back down on it that same afternoon, because that is where the tub goes.
cards.0789: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a length of scaffold board standing proud of the face of her shed door under a beech, and means to plane it and screw it tight; her sister takes the board out, lets in a new stile and a board of the thickness that belongs in it, and puts the felt back over the shed; the door shuts without being lifted for the first time since the summer, and the barrow goes back against that door that afternoon because that is where the barrow lives.
cards.0790: At the lock-up a woman in her late forties has the old kerbstone across the top of her ramp making a step, and means to take it out; the woman who books work will not, and bolts a rubber nosing over the edge of the kerbstone instead; the trolley rides up over it without stopping and the two goes become one, and she stops pulling it, and the day she does, it comes off the top of the ramp on its own and goes across the bay.
cards.0791: At number twelve a woman of seventy-eight has a flue that has not been swept since before she came, and means to get a rod up it; her sister takes the job at the kitchen hearth on the floor with a rod, a coil of rope and a flue brush, works the rope up and down the whole length twice and brings down three times the soot that was standing in it, and finds nothing else up there; the flue is the best it has been in her lifetime, and she lights the paraffin stove beside it and the smoke comes back into the room, because the flue is not what is wrong.
cards.0792: At the unit a man in his early forties has a quarter of an inch of daylight along the head of his store door and means to fill it; the woman from two doors down puts a length of brush weather strip into the head of it and screws the stop down on it; the door shuts with nothing coming through it, and inside a month he stops shutting it, because the store is only ever opened and never shut and the strip was never the problem.
cards.0793: At number nine a woman in her late fifties has a coal hole with a good new lid on it and a load standing in it that has to be aired in the frost, and means to take the lid off herself and put it back on after; the woman who does her shopping comes and takes it off in the frost and puts it back on after, which is exactly what was said in the autumn; and then she is not asked in again, and does it herself, wrong, in the wet.
cards.0794: At number ten a woman in her early thirties has a sack of gravel standing in the shed since May with a shovelful gone out of it, and means to put it down on the path; her sister opens it, puts it down and rakes it level; the path is the best it has been since she came, and she fills the sack with the topsoil that came out of the same bucket last spring and leaves a hole in it that stays in it until the sack is finished.

movement: Ten jobs, ten good methods, no hole in any of them, and ten faults that are in the people. 0785 the bed of the step brought down onto the chassis rail leaves the hinge carrying nothing, and the step is packed again inside a month by hand with whatever is to hand. 0786 four feet of wall rebuilt dry from the bottom of the footing with every perpend packed, and four bricks taken off the top course again three weeks later because chippings are showing. 0787 a post taken to the bottom of the hole and packed dry and pinned with two hardwood wedges, and the same post going over at hip height by the spring because he shuts the gate hard every time. 0788 a bay taken up and relaid on a new bed true to the flags either side, and a tub of iron put back down on it the same afternoon. 0789 a new stile and a board of the thickness that belongs in it let into the shed door, and a barrow put back against it the same afternoon. 0790 a strip of rubber bolted over the edge of the kerbstone so the trolley rides over the nose in one movement, and the hand taken off the handle, and the trolley coming off the top of the ramp on its own. 0791 a flue swept at the hearth on the floor with a rod and a coil of rope and three times the soot brought down, and the only thing that will ever go up that flue again being a stove lit out in the yard. 0792 a brush weather strip screwed into the head of a store door that is then never shut again. 0793 a coal hole aired by somebody else for the last time, and then by the woman herself in the wet. 0794 a sack of gravel raked level on a path, and the same sack filled with topsoil with the hole still in it so that it can never stand up again. Every job is dry work and every job is done from the ground.
closing_images: Ten different ones. NOT ONE OF THE TEN IS A THING PUT AWAY AND NOT ONE IS A THING LEFT WHERE IT IS, on the narrow reading settled by the read-back of 0058, where a thing left where it is means an object that was to be moved, worked on or taken away and was not, and a fault the adopted method made in the course of the chapter and nobody undid is not one. 0785 the step packed on a strip of old belting by her own hands and the new hinge carrying a load nobody pushed through it. 0786 four bricks of the top course back down dry with the perpends running open. 0787 the post going over at the height of his hip a second time. 0788 one plane of path from the front door to the gate with a tub of iron standing on the middle of it. 0789 a new stile taking the weight of a barrow that is not meant to be leaned on it. 0790 a trolley coming off the top of the ramp on its own and going across the bay. 0791 the best flue in her lifetime with a stove burning out in a yard and nothing going up it. 0792 a brush strip in the head of a door that stands open all winter. 0793 a woman on her knees at a coal hole in the wet with the lid off it and nobody coming. 0794 the rake marks in gravel and a sack in the shed with a hole in it that has no bottom to stand on. THE DEPART-AND-DO-NOT-FOLLOW GESTURE IS IN 0788 AND 0793 ONLY. A departure out of a gate is in 0786 and 0794.

prohibitions_honoured.no_arithmetic_engine: Nothing is added up, nothing is priced, nothing is counted and no number is asked to agree with another. There is no figure-mismatch spread and no telephone. No tap is run and no water is drawn, carried, poured or emptied anywhere in the ten.
prohibitions_honoured.furniture: At most ordinary domestic pairs are used as furniture. No measurement, price, room tally or mismatch is the engine of any chapter.
prohibitions_honoured.standing_objects_untouched: The freeholder does not arrive. The line is not put right. The ladder is not opened. The box behind the lock-up bench is not opened and nothing is asserted about its lid either way. The drawer with leads and screws is not opened. The drawer at ten stays shut with the hammer, the screwdriver and the paper with three lines on it. The front room at number twelve is not entered. The report is not chased. The envelope is not turned. The bowl stays on its shelf and the ring on the tiles. No felt is nailed. No ply is nailed at number ten. The gate at twelve stays propped. The sash at twelve stays a hand's width low for good. The slab at nine stays tilting to the rail. Nothing is carried between people and nothing is passed from one to another. Every job is dry work and every job is done from the ground, and no job in the ten goes on a roof, up a ladder, into a loft or into a manhole.
prohibitions_honoured.the_staple_at_the_unit: THE STAPLE ON THE GATE FRAME AT THE UNIT IS NOT DONE IN THIS BLOCK. The man from the cottage said it wants April and April is not on the page, no card stands on it, and the latch stays hooked back over the gate in both 0787 and 0792.
prohibitions_honoured.the_ply_of_0789: The ply at number ten is the sheet leaning against the shed front, unnailed, and it is not touched in 0789 or in 0794. The ply in the lock-up bay floor with a groove cut in it is a different sheet and is in a line in 0785 and 0790.
prohibitions_honoured.the_coal_hole_wood: In 0793 the load standing in the coal hole is not looked into, not counted and not carried out, and the green furry middle found in 0768 is not mentioned. The fault is in the woman opening it in the wet, not in anything about the wood.
prohibitions_honoured.wet_jobs: None. 0786, 0787 and 0791 were printed in an earlier version as a footing course, a concrete post and a roof, and all three have been rewritten dry and from the ground, so that this block's inheritance from 0784 is one flag and not four.
prohibitions_honoured.one_edge_one_visitor: One visitor at one edge per chapter at most in all ten. No chapter has a second visitor and no chapter has a visitor at two edges.

measures.said: Cap of five across the ten and at or below five in every chapter.

still_live_and_taken_up_by_nobody_here: Four pallets with the blocks in the middle of every one of them wet through. Three boards down a muddy path and a hole digging itself out at a shed corner. A coal hole with a green furry middle in it. A sheet of kitchen floor with its uncut edge across a doorway. A gate that shuts behind two wedges and stands open in front of them. A cowl on an air brick and a damp patch coming up the wall behind it. A sheet of ply with a groove cut in it. A bay of paving standing proud with a line of grit along its foot. A back door out of line with itself by a hand's width. A pipe in the middle of a wall that knocks hollow behind the packing. Three lengths of dead hedge and a barrow that does not go through. NONE OF THESE IS A MYSTERY, NONE OF THEM IS GOING TO BE ONE, AND NONE OF THEM KNOWS ABOUT ANY OF THE OTHERS. Off the page and waiting on the man off the ring road, who has now sat out four blocks: a figure for four rooms given aloud twice in a lock-up and written nowhere; a frame out of square which its own man will find at the fitting; a landing wall with a bare patch on it and a mirror in a van; a fourth room at the top of a stair that nobody has priced or looked into. Three lines of paper shut in a drawer on purpose with the tools that would do them. A box in a corner of a lock-up whose lid is not nailed.

calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.what_this_is: Six arithmetic errors in the calendar key above, found on 2 October 2026 by re-deriving every figure off the dates table and the real January and February 2023 calendars. The dates table itself was not wrong: all ten dates are real, all ten weekdays are right, none falls on the ninth or the eleventh, no two share a date, and every gap is three to seven. What was wrong was the row of gaps and the two spans printed beside it, which did not agree with the table they were supposed to describe, and a writer told to take the ladder off the real calendar would have been handed a row that puts 0785 seven days after 0784.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.the_gap_row: The key carried [7, 3, 3, 4, 4, 6, 6, 3, 3, 5]. The row off the dates table is [4, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 6, 6, 3, 5]. Four places were wrong: the incoming gap was printed as seven where 0784 to 0785 is four, the fourth and the fifth gaps were each one day out, and the eighth was one day out. The corrected row is in the key above.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.the_two_spans: From 0784 the key said forty-five days to Thursday the twenty-third of February 2023 and printed 7+3+3+4+4+6+6+3+3+5 beside it, which is forty-four and not forty-five, and the tenth chapter of the table is Monday the twentieth of February 2023. The span is forty-one days to Monday the twentieth, and the corrected addition is printed with it. From 0785 the key said thirty-eight days to the same wrong Thursday; the span is thirty-seven days to Monday the twentieth.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.the_two_bounds: Both bounds were sound and both still hold: nine gaps of three to seven from 0784 span thirty to seventy days, so Thursday 9 February to Tuesday 21 March 2023, and nine gaps of twenty-seven to sixty-three from the floor of 14 January give Friday 10 February to Saturday 18 March 2023. Both keys then named Thursday the twenty-third of February as the chapter they had to contain, which was not the chapter in the table. Monday the twentieth of February is inside both, so no bound was wrong and only the reference was.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.the_weekday_count: The key said SEVEN distinct weekdays, listed six, and then said no weekday appears three times in the block. Off the weekday array there are six, and Monday appears three times, in 0788, 0791 and 0794. The count and the sentence are corrected. The correction does not move a date: no weekday appearing more than twice was ever a rule of this block, it was a claim about one allocation, and if a writer wants it true one of those three dates moves inside the bounds.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.the_floor: The floor string above is left as it was written, because it was true when it was written, and a sentence has been added to it saying that the four-day incoming gap is spent and that 0786's own floor is Tuesday the seventeenth of January 2023.
calendar_arithmetic_corrected_2026_10_02.nothing_else_was_touched: The dates table, the weekday array, the month change, the ninth-and-eleventh check, the no-two-share check and the derivation narrative are all unchanged, because they are all correct.
